column1: # THE PREDICTION — two limbs, because p376 proved NEW ADDRESS and NEW AGENT ROW are different
# measurements (its leg returned 3 NEW and 0 agents).  A successor must be able to see that
# this pass did not collapse them after the fact.

column2: The four in-language legs TOGETHER return at least 3 addresses that `carried` grades NEW.  The Chinese leg alone returns at least 1.  I.e. J3 EXTENDS to supply: query language is a real instrument axis, and the English-index reading of the three prior zeros was partly an artefact.

Of those NEW addresses, AT MOST 1 clears this base's bar for a row on agents/top.md.  I.e. the agent-shelf zero is a property of the SHELF'S BAR (permissive grant + maintained + actually an agent), not of the index's language.

All four in-language legs return a carried set IDENTICAL to the English control — 0 NEW addresses across all four.  Then English saturation and industry saturation are THE SAME THING here, J3 is a property of policy text only, and the zero on agents/top.md is a fact about education AI rather than about the query.

2 or more of the NEW addresses clear the agent-row bar.  Then the bar was never what was holding the shelf at zero, and every "saturated" verdict from p373 onward is an artefact of query LANGUAGE, exactly as p376 feared.
Language is an instrument axis for supply AND the shelf bar is what produces the zero.  These are independent findings and the pass must publish both, not the more flattering one.

The strongest result available to this pass: it would RETIRE the language hypothesis for supply and licence a successor to stop paying for in-language supply legs.  Recorded here so a successor can check this pass did not retro-fit the outcome it wanted.
